item.text: I’m doing a smaller architectural pass rather than inventing another abstraction for its own sake: the simulator currently recomputes population analysis multiple times and doesn’t keep a coherent “current snapshot” of state. I’m consolidating that so one snapshot is the source of truth for viability and rendering.

Refactored the simulator to treat the current snapshot as the source of truth instead of recomputing analysis ad hoc. [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R007_module_java/Simulator.java:35) now keeps a `currentSnapshot`, uses it for viability in the simulation loop at [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R007_module_java/Simulator.java:80), and rebuilds it in one place through `createSnapshot()` at [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R007_module_java/Simulator.java:171). That removes repeated population analysis calls and makes simulator control flow depend on one coherent state object.

I also pushed viability onto the snapshot itself in [SimulationSnapshot.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R007_module_java/SimulationSnapshot.java:62), which keeps the simulator’s loop logic simpler and better aligned with the render-state model you already have.

Verified with `javac *.java`. No automated tests exist beyond compilation.
